chapter_theme: Invocation of God (கடவுள் வாழ்த்து): Siva, often named Nandi, is one and many, beyond the gods who cannot measure him and without equal, yet near to those who love him; the chapter urges praise in any form and promises that grace answers it.
structure_note: The chapter opens with a number verse (1) and a declaration of what the poet will sing (2). Verses 5 to 23 set Siva above and beyond the gods, the elements and the worlds; from about 24 the stress shifts to praise, worship and its fruit, often in the refrain 'praise him, and if you praise...' (25, 26, 35, 36, 39). It closes on the poet's own worship (44, 48, 50) and on crossing beyond pasu and pasam (49).

1.reading: He is one; he is two with his sweet grace; he stood within three, knew four, conquered five, spread out as six, went up beyond seven, and remains, knowing eight.
1.nuance: The verse is a count from one to eight and names almost none of what is counted. Traditionally: two as Siva with Shakti (his grace), three as the three gods or the three gunas, four as the Vedas, five as the senses, six as the six adhvas or the Vedangas, seven as the worlds above, eight as the eight qualities or the eightfold form. Only ஐந்து வென்றனன் (conquered five) and இன்னருள் (sweet grace) are fairly secure.

2.reading: Praising him, I tell of the pure one in whom dear life abides, the lord of the four directions and of the good lady, who became king even over the southern quarter by kicking Death.
2.nuance: கூற்றுதைத்தான் recalls the legend of Siva kicking Yama to save Markandeya. The south is Yama's direction, which is why தென் திசைக்கொரு வேந்தன் is taken this way; மேற்றிசைக்குள் (within the western, or the upper, quarter) is unclear.

3.reading: I enter in and meditate and praise every day the Supreme who stands alike in all, whom the undying gods hail as the naked one, and whom even those who stand at his side do not know.
3.nuance: நக்கன் (the naked one) is a name of Siva as the bare ascetic. ஒக்க நின்றான் may mean 'stands equally in everything' or 'stands together' (with Shakti). The verse sets those near him who fail to know him against the poet who enters within (புக்கு நின்று).

4.reading: Bowing and praising day and night the truth of those on the wide earth, the seed of the cosmos, who sent me into refuge with him, I stood free of darkness in the very place of strife.
4.nuance: போதவிட்டான் can be 'sent me forth' or, from போதம் (knowledge), 'made me understand'. இருள் (darkness) is traditionally the soul's root impurity (anava). இகலிடம், the place of strife, is taken as this world of birth.

5.reading: Search as you may, there is no god equal to Siva and no one here like him; the lotus-bearer with burning matted hair flashes with golden light beyond the worlds.
5.nuance: The claim is exclusive: not that Siva is highest among gods but that none compares. தாமரையான் is unusual for Siva and may mean one who wears the lotus, or one whose feet are lotuses.

6.reading: Apart from him there are no gods, no hard penance, nothing the three can achieve, and I know no way to enter the city.
6.nuance: The three (மூவர்) are usually Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra. ஊர் புகுமாறு, the way to enter the city, is traditionally taken as reaching release or Siva's world; a plain reading is possible but makes little sense here.

7.reading: He is elder to the three who are ancient alike, the chief with nothing like him; call him father and he is father too, the one of knowledge who shines like gold.
7.nuance: போதகத்தான் is taken as the one of knowledge (போதகம்), though போதகம் can also mean a young elephant. தன்னை அப்பா எனில் அப்பனுமாய் உளன: he becomes to the worshipper what the worshipper calls him.

8.reading: He is hotter than fire and cooler than water, yet no one knows the Lord's grace; far off, yet near to those who love well, the one with hanging matted hair is kinder than a mother.
8.nuance: சேயினும் நல்லன் can mean 'better than a child' or, with சேய் as 'distant', 'far beyond'; the second pairs with அணியன் (near). The opposites (hot and cool, far and near) say that grace is unknown not because it is hidden but because it is both at once.

9.reading: The one who sits with matted hair shining behind him like twisted gold is named Nandi; he is our Lord whom I worship, and there is none whom he worships.
9.nuance: Nandi here is a name of Siva, as throughout the chapter; Tirumular also calls his teacher Nandi, and the two are not always easy to separate.

10.reading: He himself bears the great earth and stands as the sky; he is the burning fire, the sun and the moon; he stands as the lady who pours rain; he is the great mountain and the cool sea.
10.nuance: தானே opens every line: he is these things, not only their maker. மழைபொழி தையல் (the rain-pouring lady) is taken as Shakti, so his consort too is a form of him.

11.reading: Look at our First One near and around, and there is no great god to compare; the end of every effort is there too; the great Nandi is the rain-pouring cloud.
11.nuance: முயலும் முயலில் முடிவும் மற்றாங்கே is compressed: the goal of all striving is in him. அயலும் புடையும் (near and around) may also mean other gods and those beside him.

12.reading: While the god with the eye in his forehead remains in one love, many say countless gods have died; those who go to the earth and those who reach the sky do not know that he is the Lord.
12.nuance: The contrast is between the gods who die and Siva who stays. ஒரு காதலின் நிற்க (stays in one love, or one desire) is unclear: perhaps his unchanging love for souls.

13.reading: Vishnu who measured the earth, Brahma of the flower and the other gods, even measuring with thought, still cannot conceive the Lord; no one has measured above him who measured the sky; measured by the eye, he stands beyond everything.
13.nuance: The verse plays on அளத்தல் (measuring) and recalls the legend of the column of fire whose top and bottom Brahma and Vishnu could not find. விண்ணளந்தான் may be Vishnu again (who measured the sky) or Siva.

14.reading: He stands beyond the lotus-born one, beyond our dark sea-coloured Mayan, beyond even what lies past them; the Lord stands beyond everywhere and stands seeing all.
14.nuance: கடந்துநின்றான் (stood beyond) opens every line. The last words, கண்டுநின்றான், balance transcendence with presence: beyond all, he still watches all.

15.reading: As the First and as Hara, as the transformer standing within the body, he spread and filled and remained; as the light of grace and as justice in a nature that never shrinks, he stands eternal.
15.nuance: வேதி is taken as the one who transforms (as alchemy changes metal), or as the Vedic one; the first fits உடலுள் நின்ற, within the body. The verse places the Lord in the body as well as beyond the world, a theme the later tantras develop.

16.reading: The immortals and the gods, delighting in the one with konrai in his matted hair who shares half his body with the bright-browed lady, practise his qualities.
16.nuance: கோது குலாவிய recurs in lines 1 and 4 and is obscure: கோது can mean dross, fault or a flower's sheath, so the last line may say the gods, for all their worship, still cling to faults. யாது குலாவி (delighting in what?) may be a question.

17.reading: Even if asafoetida and the like are boiled together with it, musk's scent prevails; in the same way, even if one mixes with the gods of many lands and thinks of one as god, nothing equals kinship with the Lord.
17.nuance: காயம் is read as asafoetida, set against கத்தூரி (musk); it can also mean the body. இரண்டும் and மாயம் are hard to fit, and the simile's point (the stronger scent wins) is a reading.

18.reading: Seeing the full penance of the king of Alaka, our Lord made him overlord and lord of wealth, and said: if you cherish that lordship and make it prosper, take this lordship.
18.nuance: The king of Alaka is Kubera, made lord of wealth by Siva for his penance. The speech in the last two lines is compressed and its sense uncertain.

19.reading: The one of ancient wisdom, who made the seven groves fragrant with cardamom an ancient seat, seeing the true penance of the one he made lord, dwells there as that seat.
19.nuance: The verse continues 18 (இதுபதி) and plays on பதி as lord and as place. விதுபதி may be the moon's lord or a misreading; who did the penance and which seat is meant are unclear.

20.reading: If you seek the path of virtue where the Lord dwells who first created death and birth, thunder and its roar are the Lord's form, and it is the mountain of fragrant flowers.
20.nuance: The second half is obscure. கடிமலர்க் குன்ற மலை may be Kailasa or a particular hill; the thunder as his form may echo the rain imagery of 10 and 11.

21.reading: Praise the king who tore the forest elephant so that it screamed, the One who ends the flawed birth of Vishnu dark as a great cloud, of Brahma and of the gods, and you may join him.
21.nuance: The elephant is the demon Siva flayed (Gajasura). ஊனப் பிறவி (flawed, or fleshly, birth) puts even the high gods inside the round of births from which only Siva frees.

22.reading: The good lord of the land of maya, who rises within the mind, knows what one thinks; yet people do not think of him and say 'the Lord has no love for me', while the Lord stands caring for those who would be saved.
22.nuance: பிழைக்க நின்றார் can be 'those who stand to be saved' or 'those who stand in error'; on the second reading, his care reaches even the wrongdoers. The complaint that God has no love is answered: it is people who do not think of him.

23.reading: Do not say there is no Lord: the mighty one, just Lord who made the elephant stop at his word, first of the gods, gives grace by night and day.
23.nuance: The first line (வன்னிக்கு இறையிடை வாரணம்) refers to a legend I can't identify; வன்னி may be fire or the vanni tree. இல்லென வேண்டா, 'don't say he is not', is plain.

24.reading: Praise and laud the holy one's feet and grow clear; the wealth is always Siva's feet; he stays firm in the way of those who have turned back the mind that was deluded.
24.nuance: The middle is compressed: 'wealth is Siva's feet' revalues செல்வம். ஆற்றியதென்று மயலுற்ற சிந்தை may be the mind deluded by thinking it has achieved something.

25.reading: Worship the unborn, deathless, never-departing one, the bearer of the bow, great in grace, who gives joy to all; if you worship, the never-forgetting one becomes for you an undying greatness.
25.nuance: A string of -இலி names (பிறப்பிலி, இறப்பிலி, துறப்பிலி, மறப்பிலி: without birth, death, leaving, forgetting). மாயா விருத்தம் is unclear: 'unperishing greatness' or 'the state free of maya'.

26.reading: Worship the one who follows you; if you worship, he spreads through all the earth, stands beyond, above the lotus flower, and dwelling with him is the merit of his feet.
26.nuance: தொடர்ந்துநின்றான் (who follows, or stays with, the soul) is a mark of grace. கடந்துநின்றாம் (we stood beyond) is probably கடந்துநின்றான் (he stood beyond), as in 14; the lotus may be Brahma's or the heart's.

27.reading: Those who bow daily to Nandi, saying 'the grace of the endless Lord with the bright lotus face, fit to be called the meeting-point, is for us', he enters and stays within their minds.
27.nuance: சந்தி (twilight, or a junction) is unclear; it may be the dawn-and-dusk hour of worship. The verse's claim is plain: he enters the minds of those who bow to him.

28.reading: He stands in accord and has become everything; he stands apart and has become before and behind; the lord of Amaravati stands withered; to those who stand bowing he is a companion on the way.
28.nuance: இணங்கி / பிணங்கி (agreeing, opposing) give the Lord both relations to the world. The lord of Amaravati is Indra; உணங்கி நின்றான் may say Indra stands humbled before Siva, or it may describe Siva, which is harder to make sense of.

29.reading: Stand where I can see you: who else is kin to me, your servant? I will not hold back in shame from embracing you. He has settled as the linchpin in the minds of devotees whose nature never bends.
29.nuance: The first two lines address the Lord directly, the last two speak of him. ஆணி (nail, linchpin, or the finest gold) makes him what holds the devotee's mind in place.

30.reading: Some hesitate, wondering whether the Lord, like rain calling from the sky, will call them from where he stands; as the cow stands and calls, I stand and call my Nandi, seeking knowledge.
30.nuance: The two images are set against each other: waiting to be called down from above, and calling out oneself as a cow lows for its calf (or a calf for its mother; ஆன் can be either). The poet calls ஞானம் கருதி, wanting knowledge, not reward.

31.reading: He is the same on earth, in the sky, in the heavens and in the Veda; for him who took to singing sweet music in melody, I stood in my eye and loved.
31.nuance: கண்ணகத்தே நின்று can be read as the Lord standing within the eye or the poet loving with his whole sight. Sengalvaraya notes the same phrase in Tiruvasagam (Tiruppalliyezhuchi 9).

32.reading: The lord of the gods, our lord, who fills the ten directions and strides across the seven worlds of spreading water: no one knows his nature, and to praise the all-pervading lord becomes a song of grace.
32.nuance: பிரான் closes each half-line. The last line may mean that singing of him is itself grace, or that he is reached through songs of grace.

33.reading: Of old this world had many lords; people perform many rites and do not see the one truth; even those who can recite many praises and hymns lack understanding and wither within.
33.nuance: A check on the chapter's own call to praise: hymns and rites without understanding (மதி) leave the heart withered. பதிபல may be many gods or many cities and shrines; விதி பல may be rules or rites.

34.reading: Like the scent the sandal-fragrant yak-tail fan carries, the true way the king gave the gods and his thousand names, like a full flame, I praise whether going or sitting.
34.nuance: The simile is hard to fix: the scent may be the true way, which spreads like the fan's fragrance, or the names. போந்தும் இருந்தும் (going and staying) means at all times.

35.reading: Praise the Lord who is the way when no way avails; praise and laud him, and if you laud him he will change you, through the eight directions with west and east, and set you dancing so.
35.nuance: ஆற்றுகிலா வழி (the way for those unable to cope, or the way one cannot achieve oneself) and the last two lines are obscure. மாற்றுவன் may be 'transform you' or 'turn you about'; ஆட்டவுமாம் may speak of the soul made to dance as Siva dances.

36.reading: Praise in whatever way you can the father, Nandi, the nectar one never tires of, the peerless giver, the first of the aeon; if you praise him, you can win the Lord's grace in that same measure.
36.nuance: எப்பரிசாயினும் ... அப்பரிசு: grace answers praise in kind and measure. The verse lowers the bar for worship: any form will do.

37.reading: I too stand and praise Nandi every day; he too stands, his body like flame; like the moon in the sky he delights within the body and stands in the flesh, and so it breathes with life.
37.nuance: உயிர்க்கின்றவாறே is read as 'that is how it lives'. The verse puts the Lord in the flesh as the source of its life, which the later tantras develop as the body as temple. The moon image may be yogic.

38.reading: I will not stop babbling of the great and rare one, of the one whose form is unborn, of our great Nandi, of the one of greatness.
38.nuance: பிதற்று is raving or babbling, the devotee's speech that does not care how it sounds; repeated at the head of each line, it enacts what it says.

39.reading: By praising the light within the minds of those able to praise, the holy one, the god who delights there, by bowing to him as our Lord and holding him dear, one can win the Lord's grace.
39.nuance: The light is already in the minds of those who praise; worship here is turning toward what is within. ஆத்தம் is taken as love or trust.

40.reading: The Lord's anklet-ringing feet, which the humbled come to seek, are like the light of pure red gold; for those who can praise without hidden guile, he enters and stays and works on the outer frame.
40.nuance: மறைஞ்சடம் is taken as concealed deceit and புறஞ்சடம் as the outer body, so the last line may mean he transforms or removes the outer body; the second half is obscure.

41.reading: For those who can praise in a heart tilled like a field the lord of the gods who swallowed the raging poison, the one who shares half his body with the bright-browed lady stays there in accord, like a deer among its herd.
41.nuance: புனஞ்செய்த நெஞ்சு, the heart made into a cleared field, is a farming image for a mind prepared to receive him; the deer at ease with its kind says he dwells there naturally.

42.reading: What those who go and praise Hara gain is what the Lord made the crown; even if they come wrapped in maya, the king of the bamboo-shouldered lady becomes one with them.
42.nuance: நாயகனான் முடி செய்ததுவே நல்கும் is obscure: perhaps the highest state, or the crown he gave others. The point that maya is no bar to praise is fairly clear.

43.reading: For those who, speaking of Hara's feet, crying and weeping, seek and meditate daily on the feet of the Supreme and can settle there, he fills them, giving his feet in order.
43.nuance: அரற்றி அழுது (crying out and weeping) is the devotional weeping of the Tamil saints. உரன் அடி செய்து and நிரன் அடி செய்து are obscure; the play on அடி runs through all four lines.

44.reading: The gods say 'praise' to the pure one's feet, the asuras say it, humans say it; I have set 'praise' to shine within my love.
44.nuance: Gods, demons and humans alike praise him; what sets the poet apart is not the word but where it is placed, inside love.

45.reading: This sea-girt world runs only by ordinance, and outside the ordinance there is neither joy nor its opposite; by the way of daily praise, the Lord of light becomes the sun that shows the way to the Lord.
45.nuance: விதி may be fate, divine ordinance or prescribed rule, and விருத்தம் the contrary of joy or something else. The verse sets the way of ordinance (விதிவழி) against the way of praise (துதிவழி) and the way to the Lord (பதிவழி).

46.reading: While devotees made worship, thinking 'you of twilight colour, Hara, Siva' and 'you of the first colour, First One, Supreme', the one whose colour is the intellect entered our mind.
46.nuance: The play on வண்ணம் (colour, form, manner) runs through the verse: the red of evening, the first, and finally புந்தி வண்ணன், one whose form is understanding.

47.reading: Those who stay in the household are equal to great ascetics; those who keep him in thought stand in his love; but like the kite perched in the palmyra, those who do not think of you have no joy of you.
47.nuance: The first line read alone equates householders with ascetics; read with the second, it may mean householders who keep the Lord in mind. The kite in the palmyra is traditionally taken as sitting by the fruit and not tasting it, or as perched without settling.

48.reading: Bowing my head to the lord of the immortals whom devotees extol, thinking of the First One, our father, the Supreme beyond the supreme who gives grace in measure, I stay with him as a lamp that needs no dawn.
48.nuance: விடியா விளக்கு is a lamp that does not go out at dawn, or one that needs no daybreak; it may describe the Lord or the poet's steady devotion. படியால் may be 'on earth' or 'in measure'.

49.reading: Those who think of the Lord of pasu and pasam and can gather themselves on the teaching of pasu and pasam will swim the rich sea of sin and reach the shore, passing beyond pasu and pasam.
49.nuance: பசு பாசம் closes the first half of every line, with நரை, உரை, திரை, கரை before it. Traditionally pasu is the soul and pasam its bonds, under pati the Lord, the three categories of Saiva Siddhanta. நரை (grey, ancient) and திரை (wave) are hard to fit.

50.reading: Calling him Lord I will wear him and keep him in my heart; I will sing, scatter many flowers, bow and dance, and dancing seek him as the lord of the immortals: this is what I know today.
50.nuance: The verse lists the acts of worship (wearing, holding, singing, scattering flowers, bowing, dancing, seeking) and ends with the modest claim that this is all he knows today.

links.note: Both invocations name God as the one who conquered the five: the Kural's one who quenched the five sense-gates, Tirumular's ஐந்து வென்றனன்.

Both invocations close on the number eight: the Kural's எண்குணத்தான், one of eight qualities, and Tirumular's உணர்ந்தெட்டே. Tradition reads both as the eight divine qualities, though Tirumular's eight may also be the eightfold form.

Both make God the one with no likeness: the Kural's தனக்குவமை இல்லாதான், Tirumular's தன்னைஒப்பாய் ஒன்றும் இல்லாத் தலைமகன். The Kural adds that only reaching his feet ends the mind's anxiety; Tirumular adds that he becomes father to whoever calls him so.

The Kural asks what learning is worth if it does not bow at God's feet; Tirumular turns the test on the worshippers, saying that even those who can recite many hymns lack understanding. Bowing is necessary in one, not enough in the other.
Both rank the householder with or above the ascetic: the Kural's virtuous household life endures more than those who do penance, Tirumular's householders are equal to great ascetics.

The Naladiyar's wise, seeing the pain in pleasure, keep off the household way; Tirumular says those who stay in the household equal great ascetics. The conflict holds if 47's first line is a general claim about householders, not only those who keep the Lord in mind.

Both picture salvation as swimming a sea: the Kural's sea of births, crossed by reaching the Lord's feet, and Tirumular's sea of sin, crossed by thinking of the Lord and reaching the shore beyond pasu and pasam.
13 says the gods cannot measure the Lord; 14 states the result in a refrain, he stands beyond Brahma, beyond Vishnu and beyond everything, yet sees all.
18 has the Lord make Kubera lord of wealth for his penance and say 'take this lordship'; 19 opens on the same இதுபதி and gives another seat granted for true penance.

Both verses praise (போற்றி) the lord of the four directions (நாற்றிசைக்கும் நாதன் / நாற்றிசைக்கும் நடுவாகின்ற நம்பன்) and name him by one deed, கூற்றுதைத்தான், the one who kicked Death. 2 is the poet announcing what he will tell; 2105, in the chapter of counsel, turns the same formula outward: tell his nature and be saved (கூறிநின்று உய்ம்மினே). The near-repeat shows the invocation's praise returning as the means of salvation.

3 sets those who stand at his side (பக்கநின்றார்) and do not know him against the poet who enters within and meditates (புக்குநின்று உன்னி). 1739 says that described in other words he stands beyond them, and that apart from the gods whose work is lofty speech he has entered my mind (என் மனம் புகுந்தானே). The later verse fills out the contrast: nearness and speech fail where entering the mind succeeds.

4 ends with the poet standing free of darkness (இருள் நீங்கி நின்றேனே) through bowing and praising day and night. Kural 352 promises the same removal of darkness (இருள்நீங்கி இன்பம் பயக்கும்) to those of stainless sight who have left confusion. The same phrase is reached by worship in one and by true seeing in the other.

5 says that search as you may there is no god equal to Siva and no one like him (சிவனொடு ஒக்கும் தெய்வம் தேடினும் இல்லை). Kural 7 names God by the same claim, தனக்குவமை இல்லாதான், the one with no likeness. Tirumular makes the Kural's title the outcome of a search and gives it a name.

6 says that without him there are no gods, no rare penance, nothing the three can do, and no way to enter the city (அவனன்றி ஊர்புகுமாறு அறியேனே). 1053 repeats the verse almost word for word with Shakti as subject (அவளன்றி ஊர்புகும் ஆறறியேனே), and the five in place of the three. The near-repeat shows the book giving the Lord's sole sufficiency to his Shakti in the same words.

6 knows no way to enter the city apart from him (அவனன்றி ஊர்புகுமாறு அறியேனே). Kural 8 says that except for those who reach the feet of the sea of virtue, the other seas are hard to swim (தாள்சேர்ந்தார்க் கல்லால் பிறவாழி நீந்தல் அரிது). Both state the goal as reachable only through him, one as entering a city, the other as crossing a sea.

8 says the Lord with hanging matted hair is kinder than a mother (தாயினும் நல்லன்) and near to those who love well. 116 uses the same comparison for what he does: Nandi, dwelling in the body as temple, removes the three malas more tenderly than a mother (தாயினும் மும்மலம் மாற்றி). The invocation's epithet becomes in 116 a description of grace at work on the soul.

9 says Nandi is the Lord whom the poet worships and there is no one whom he himself worships (தன்னால் தொழப்படுவார் இல்லை). Thiruppugazh 156 opens by praising Murugan as the guru who spoke the instructing mantra into both of Siva's ears (சிவனார் மனங்குளிர உபதேச மந்த்ரம் இரு செவிமீதிலும் பகர் குருநாதா). The conflict holds if being a disciple puts Siva below one he reveres; it softens if Murugan is taken as Siva's own form.

11 ends by calling great Nandi the rain-pouring cloud (பெயலும் மழைமுகில் பேர்நந்தி). Kural 11 says the world keeps going by the rain from the sky (வான்நின்று உலகம் வழங்கி வருதலால்), so rain is amrita. The Kural's praise of rain as what sustains the world becomes in Tirumular a name of the Lord.

12 sets the countless gods who are said to have died (எண்ணிலி தேவர் இறந்தார்) against the Lord who stays, and says those of earth and sky do not know he is the Lord. 762 gives the way to that knowledge: look within the things that pass with the mind fixed (கழிகின்ற உள்ளே கருத்துற நோக்கில்) and the thing that does not pass can be seen. The pairing turns 12's complaint about not knowing into a method.

13 says Vishnu, Brahma and the gods cannot conceive the Lord and no one has measured above him (மேலளந்தார் இல்லை), alluding to the search for his top. 88 tells the story outright: Brahma and Vishnu sought foot and crown (அடிமுடி காண்பார்) and failed, and Brahma lied that he saw the crown. 13 uses the legend as a figure of measuring; 88 adds the lie.

14 ranks the Lord step by step beyond Brahma and beyond Vishnu (கடந்துநின்றான் கமலம் மலராதி, கடந்துநின்றான் ... மாயன்). 110 says the ignorant do not know the one great light stood as three and as five, and babble, dividing it into Isan, tall Mal and Brahma (ஈசன் நெடுமால் அயனென்று பேதித்து). If 14 is read as ranking three separate beings, 110 calls that division ignorance; if 14 means the one light exceeds its own forms, they agree.

15 places the Lord as the one standing within the body (உடலுள் நின்ற வேதி) as well as spreading through all. 3028 says that living in the body and seeking the light within (உள்ளொளி நாடி), one can see the god who dwells inside the body (உடலிடை வைகின்ற உள்ளுறு தேவன்) as plainly as the sea's waves. The invocation's claim at the book's opening returns near its end as something one can see.

17 uses musk (கத்தூரி), whose scent prevails over what is boiled with it, as the figure for kinship with the Lord that nothing equals. 1459 says the fragrance of Siva (சிவமணம்) has blossomed within the soul as scent dwells in a flower, and ends on the central post joined with musk (நாவி அணைந்த நடுதறி). Both make the Lord a scent that cannot be overpowered; 17's simile is uncertain, so the pairing rests on the shared figure.

21 calls the Lord the One who ends the flawed birth (ஊனப் பிறவி ஒழிக்கும் ஒருவன்) of Vishnu, Brahma and the gods, placing them inside the round of births. 107 says Brahma and Vishnu are not strangers to us but kin of Nandi, and you will gain blessing through those gods (வயனம் பெறுவீர் அவ்வானவராலே). 107 limits the downgrading in 21: born gods still carry the Lord's blessing.

22 says the Lord who rises in the mind knows what one thinks (நினைத்தது அறிவன), while people do not think of him and complain that the Lord has no love for them (எனக்கு இறை அன்பிலன்). 280 says the Lord knows what we have spurned and what we have gained (இகழ்ந்ததும் பெற்றதும் ஈசன் அறியும்) and returns love with delight to those who love. 280 answers 22's complaint: his love is given back to love.

23 says do not say he is not (இல்லென வேண்டா): the Lord gives grace night and day. 2558 says the world knows that those who say there is no higher state (பரகதி ... இல்லையென்போர்) go the way of hell. 23 forbids the denial and 2558 gives its consequence.

24 says the wealth is always Siva's feet (என்றும் சிவனடிக்கே செல்வம்) and praises those who turn back the deluded mind. 168 says that before favour, king, elephants and wealth pass to others, joining the one who is wealth (செல்வனைச் சேரின்) ends confusion and is the great penance. 168 gives the reason 24 leaves out: ordinary wealth leaves, and the Lord is the wealth that stays.

25 strings names ending in -இலி: பிறப்பிலி, இறப்பிலி, துறப்பிலி, மறப்பிலி (without birth, death, leaving, forgetting). 2941 strings the same form: உருவிலி, ஊனிலி, திருவிலி, தீதிலி, பொருவிலி, மருவிலி (without form, flesh, wealth, evil, equal, clinging). Both define the Lord by what he lacks; 25 ends in a call to worship and 2941 in his entering the mind.

26 says worship the one who follows you (தொடர்ந்துநின்றானை), who spreads through all the earth (படர்ந்துநின்றான்) and stands beyond (கடந்துநின்றாம்). 2643 uses the same three verbs: he followed me (தொடர்ந்துநின்றான்) when he tested me, spread (படர்ந்துநின்று) and, standing beyond (கடந்துநின்று), shows the way. The near-repeat confirms 26's கடந்துநின்றாம் should read as the Lord standing beyond.

28 makes the Lord the companion on the way (வழித்துணை) for those who bow. Kural 36 gives that role to virtue: do it now, for when you perish it is a companion that does not perish (பொன்றுங்கால் பொன்றாத் துணை). The same office of the one companion for the journey is filled by the Lord in one and by dharma in the other.

29 says the Lord has settled as the linchpin (ஆணியன் ஆகி) in the minds of devotees whose nature does not bend. Kural 667 says not to scorn people for their looks, since a great rolling chariot has its linchpin (உருள்பெருந்தேர்க்கு அச்சாணி). The small pin that holds the great moving thing is a person of worth in the Kural and the Lord in the devotee's mind in Tirumular.

29 makes the Lord the linchpin (ஆணி) in the minds of steadfast devotees. 2080 calls him the linchpin of the world (உலகாணி) and of the land in the five, and says the chief work toward him is knowing oneself. The same figure is used for the mind in 29 and for the world in 2080.

30 says the poet stands and calls his Nandi as a cow stands and calls (ஆன்நின்று அழைக்குமது போல்), wanting knowledge. 2446 has Nandi come like a mother rising at the thought of her calf (கன்று நினைந்தெழு தாயென வந்தபின்). The two complete one image: the devotee lows like the cow, and the Lord answers as the cow to its calf.

31 ends with the poet standing in the eye and loving him (கண்ணகத்தே நின்று காதலித்தேனே). 1505 says that for those who hold him as their eye (கண்ணவன் என்று கருதுமவர்கட்கு) the Lord stands held by great love (பேரன்பு பற்றி நின்றான்). Both join the eye with love for the Lord; 1505 turns it round, so that love holds him.

32 calls the Lord the one who fills the ten directions (திசை பத்தையும் மேவு பிரான்) and says no one knows his nature. 1451 says there is one supreme God in the ten directions and no direction where he is not (எத்திக்கு இலர் இல்லை), and turns this into refuge: take the shade of his feet and the sea of deeds will not reach you. 1451 adds what to do with the pervasion 32 praises.

35 says praise the Lord who is the way when nothing else avails (ஆற்றுகிலா வழியாகும் இறைவன்), and he will change you (மாற்றுவன்). Kural 7 says that except for those who reach the incomparable one's feet, it is hard to change the mind's distress (மனக்கவலை மாற்றல் அரிது). The Kural says the change is hard without him; Tirumular promises that he makes it.

36 says praise him in whatever way (எப்பரிசாயினும்) and you can win the Lord's grace in that same measure (அப்பரிசு ஈசன் அருள்பெறலாமே). 130 says however far one's knowing reaches (எவ்வாறு காண்பான் அறிவு தனக்கெல்லை), so far Hara gives grace (அவ்வாறு அருட்செய்வன்). Both build grace as an answer matched to the seeker, by the same எ-/அ- correlation, measured by praise in one and by knowing in the other.

37 says the Lord delights within the body and stands in the flesh (ஊனில் நின்று), and so it lives. 725 draws the consequence: once I held the body to be shameful, but seeing that the Highest has made it his temple (உடம்புளே உத்தமன் கோயில்கொண்டான்), I cherish it. 37's claim that the Lord lives in the flesh becomes in 725 a reason to care for the body.

38 repeats பிதற்றொழியேன், I will not stop babbling of great Nandi (எங்கள் பேர்நந்தி தன்னை). 94 says the same in the poet's own story: always I babble of great Nandi (பிதற்றுகின்றேன் என்றும் பேர்நந்தி தன்னை) and hold him in my heart night and day. The near-repeat makes the babbling a lasting habit, not one verse's flourish.

38 makes babbling of Nandi (பிதற்றொழியேன்) the devotee's vow. 2613 says there is no use sitting and babbling (பேசி இருந்து பிதற்றிப் பயனில்லை) about breath and the needle; cut desire and attachment (ஆசையும் அன்பும் அறுமின்) and the Lord's place is easy. The tension holds if both babblings are taken as speech about the Lord; 2613's babble is yogic talk, so the book praises one kind and dismisses the other.

39 places the light within the minds of those able to praise (வாழ்த்தவல்லார் மனத்துள்ளுறு சோதி), and says grace is won by praising and bowing. 1123 places the inner light (உள்ளொளி) of Shakti in the hearts of those who have driven out their deeds (வினைகடிந்தார் உள்ளத்து). 1123 sets a further condition on whose heart holds the light.

40 says that for those who can praise without hidden guile (மறைஞ்சடம் செய்யாது வாழ்த்தவல்லார்க்கு) the Lord enters and stays. 511 says none of the deceitful (கள்ளத்தினார்), however they mingle, know the One felt within the heart. One promises entry to the guileless; the other shuts out the guileful.

41 says the Lord dwells at ease in a heart made like a tilled field (புனஞ்செய்த நெஞ்சு) by those who praise. 1834 condemns those who carry loads of flowers outward but will not enter the sea of the heart (உள்ளக் கடற்புக்கு) and leave the sea of deceit; they sink. The pairing places worship's work inside the heart, with a farming image in one and a sea image in the other.

42 says that even if those who praise Hara come wrapped in maya (மாயகம் சூழ்ந்து வரவல்லராகிலும்), the king becomes one with them. 2421 says the Lord kindly feeds the soul through the maya he set working (பண்ணிய மாயையில் ஊட்டல் பரிந்தனன்), and grace is the means to his feet. 2421 explains why maya is no bar in 42: it is his own instrument. 42 is obscure in its first half, so the pairing rests on line 3.

43 says the Lord fills those who, speaking of Hara's feet, cry and weep (அரற்றி அழுது) and seek the Supreme's feet daily. 1552 says that if those who weep (இருந்தழுவாரும்) take up rare austerity and think of the Lord, he keeps them from suffering and there is no more birth. 1552 names the end that 43's weeping leads to.

43 promises the Lord's fullness to those who cry out and weep (அரற்றி அழுது) over Hara's feet. Thiruppugazh 1028 sends to Death's town those who never melt saying 'life of the Lord who shares his body with the woman' (மாதுபாகர் வாழ்வே யெனா நெக்குருகார்). The same melting devotion is rewarded in one and its absence punished in the other.

33 says even those able to recite many praises and hymns (துதிபல தோத்திரம் சொல்லவல்லாரும்) lack understanding and wither. 44 says gods, asuras and humans all say போற்றி, but the poet has set it to shine within his love (போற்றி என் அன்புள் பொலியவைத்தேனே). 44 names what 33's hymn-singers lack: the word of praise is the same, and love is the difference.

45 says this world runs only by ordinance (விதிவழி அல்லது இவ்வேலை உலகம்), yet by the way of praise the Lord of light becomes the sun showing the way to him. Kural 380 asks what is stronger than fate (ஊழிற் பெருவலி யாவுள), which gets there first whatever one devises. 45 grants fate's rule over the world and adds praise as a way it does not close.

46 ends with the Lord whose form is the intellect entering our mind (புந்தி வண்ணன் எம் மனம் புகுந்தான்). Kural 3 names God மலர்மிசை ஏகினான், the one who went upon the flower, which the commentators, as Pope's rendering shows, read as the flower of the mind. On that reading both place the Lord walking into the devotee's heart.

48 ends with the poet staying with the Lord as a lamp that does not dawn away (விடியா விளக்கென்று மேவிநின்றேனே). 1687 calls the inner seeing behind the strong inner eyelid the lamp that guards against the night not ending (விடியாமை காக்கும் விளக்கு). Both use விடி- with விளக்கு, one for a lamp that needs no dawn and one for a lamp that brings it.

48 holds to the Lord as a lamp that never dawns away (விடியா விளக்கு). Naladiyar 51 says austerity drives off sin as a lamp drives off darkness, but when the oil runs out darkness rushes back (விளக்குநெய் தேய்விடத்துச் சென்றிருள் பாய்ந்தாங்கு). The Naladiyar's lamp of merit fails as merit is spent; Tirumular's lamp is the one that does not.

49 promises that those who think of the Lord of pasu and pasam will cross the sea of sin and pass beyond pasu and pasam (கரைபசு பாசம் கடந்து). 115 states the doctrine behind it: pasu and pasam are beginningless like pati and cannot reach him, but when pati draws near they do not remain (பதியணுகிற் பசு பாசம் நில்லாவே). 115 explains why thinking of the Lord in 49 leads beyond the bonds.

50 lists what the poet will do: sing, scatter flowers, bow, dance (பாடுவன் ... ஆடுவன்), and says this is what he knows today. 96 says he does not know how to sing in the way of those who can sing, nor dance in the way of those who can dance (பாடவல்லார் நெறி பாட அறிகிலேன், ஆடவல்லார் நெறி ஆட அறிகிலேன்). 96 limits 50: the poet sings and dances without the skilled ways.

source_issues: 14: line 1 reads கடந்துநினின் றான், a misprint for கடந்துநின் றான்.
23: line 1 reads வன்னிககு, a misprint for வன்னிக்கு; the line's legend is obscure.
26: line 3 reads கடந்துநின் றாம் (we stood beyond), probably for கடந்துநின் றான் as in 14.
30: line 2 reads தானினறு, a misprint for தான்நின்று.
49: line 2 reads பாசததுஒருங்க, a misprint for பாசத்து ஒருங்க, and line 4 கடநது for கடந்து.
16, 17, 19, 23, 35, 40 and 43 have lines too obscure to read with confidence and may be corrupt.
